strings.help.tab.essentials: The settings people change most, in one list. Each row also stays in its own tab. The last row lets you choose which rows appear here.
strings.help.tab.look: How the home row looks and behaves: theme, icons, app names, spacing, where the highlight starts and quiet mode.
strings.help.tab.clock: The clock, date and weather on the home screen. A live preview shows while the widget is on.
strings.help.tab.wallpaper: The picture behind the apps: a built-in background, your own pictures or a slideshow, and how it is shown.
strings.help.tab.saver: A screen saver of your own, for rooted TVs (experimental): what plays, for how long and how it protects an OLED screen.
strings.help.tab.system: Language, updates, how Home and other remote buttons open Hearth, what starts with the TV, and uninstalling Hearth.
strings.help.group.Theme: Colours of the tiles, text and background. Your own looks can be saved as themes.
strings.help.group.Icons: Size, shape, style, colour and spacing of the app icons on the home row.
strings.help.group.Home row: How the home row is laid out and scrolls, where the highlight starts, and which extra tiles it shows.
strings.help.group.Labels: The app names under the icons: show or hide them, and set their colour, font, size and thickness.
strings.help.group.Quiet mode: After a pause with no key press the apps hide, so only the wallpaper shows. Any key brings them back. It can also dim the screen, switch the TV off later and shift the clock and apps slightly against burn-in.
strings.help.group.Favourites: Spacing of the favourites row. While favourites are set, only that row shows; Down shows the full row.
strings.help.group.Recent apps: The panel that opens when you press Back on the home screen.
strings.help.group.Remote control: The Home button and other remote buttons. Needs root; Hearth uses its bundled key hook, so no other tool is needed. Map the Home button first, then other keys, and use the pointer block only if the Magic Remote pointer gets in the way.
strings.help.group.TV start: What happens when the TV starts or Home is pressed: replacing LG Home (the Home button, the helper or a stand-in), an app at power-on, a TV input entry and the LG logo. Use one Home replacement at a time; the Home button is the cleanest.
strings.help.group.Memory: Experimental ways to keep Hearth or LG apps loaded so they open faster. They use the memory of the TV, so leave them off unless your TV has memory to spare and a slow start bothers you.
strings.help.pref.iconScale: Makes the app icons on the home row larger or smaller.
strings.help.pref.rows: Shows the apps in one row or split over two rows.
strings.help.pref.tileShape: The outline of every app icon: rounded, square, circle and more.
strings.help.pref.showLabels: Shows or hides the app names under the icons.
strings.help.pref.labelColor: The colour of the app names.
strings.help.pref.labelFont: The typeface of the app names.
strings.help.pref.labelSize: How large the app names are.
strings.help.pref.labelWeight: How thick the app names are.
strings.help.pref.theme: The colours of tiles, text and background. Arrows browse your saved themes; the preview shows the result.
strings.help.pref.themeExport: Writes theme_base.zip into the themes folder (/media/developer/themes): a ready starting point for your own theme. It already holds your apps in their present order, their names and their icons. Copy it to a computer, change colours, fonts, names or icons in its manifest.json (or hand it to an AI helper together with the theme guide that is inside the zip), zip it again and copy it back. Then pick it under Current theme (OK loads a zip). Parts you leave out change nothing, so you can make a theme of only colours or only icons. Needs a rooted TV.
strings.help.pref.iconStyle: How the icons are drawn: the original artwork, one-colour shapes, or artwork on a themed tile. Experimental.
strings.help.pref.iconLight: Dark tiles with light shapes, or light tiles with dark shapes. Only for the one-colour styles.
strings.help.pref.iconColor: The colour of the one-colour icon shapes: the theme's own or a plain colour.
strings.help.pref.iconOpacity: Lower values let the wallpaper show through the icons.
strings.help.pref.sideMargin: The space left and right of the app row.
strings.help.pref.bottomMargin: The space between the app row and the bottom of the screen.
strings.help.pref.favSideMargin: The space left and right of the favourites row.
strings.help.pref.favBottomMargin: The space below the favourites row while it is alone. Raise it for a higher row.
strings.help.pref.inputStatus: Unplugged inputs are greyed out, and a connected device's name shows under its tile. Rooted TVs.
strings.help.pref.showLgHome: Adds a tile that opens LG's own Home screen.
strings.help.pref.showSystem: Adds a tile that opens the TV's own settings.
strings.help.pref.hideSettings: Hides the Hearth Settings tile. Hold OK on an app and choose Hearth Settings to get in.
strings.help.pref.clockFormat: 12-hour, 24-hour, or the same as the TV.
strings.help.pref.showPeriod: Shows AM or PM beside the time. Only in 12-hour format.
strings.help.pref.showDate: Shows the day and date under the time.
strings.help.pref.clockSize: How large the time is. The date and weather scale with it.
strings.help.pref.clockFont: The typeface of the time, date and weather.
strings.help.pref.clockWeight: How thick the time and date are.
strings.help.pref.clockTop: How far the widget sits from the top of the screen.
strings.help.pref.clockLeft: Where the widget sits from left to right. 50% is the centre.
strings.help.pref.clockAlign: Lines the time, date and weather up left, centre or right of the widget's position.
strings.help.pref.clockColor: The colour of the time, date and weather. Follow theme keeps the theme's own.
strings.help.pref.clockShadow: A soft shadow so the widget reads on bright pictures.
strings.help.pref.clockScrim: A soft glow behind the widget so it reads on any picture. Dark behind light text, light behind dark text.
strings.help.pref.clockOpacity: How solid the time, date and weather are.
strings.help.pref.weatherOn: Shows the temperature and conditions under the date. Needs internet.
strings.help.pref.weatherCity: The city the weather is for. Opens the city list.
strings.help.pref.weatherCityName: Puts the city name before the temperature.
strings.help.pref.weatherRange: Adds today's high and low, for example H 31 L 25.
strings.help.pref.updates: Looks for a newer Hearth and offers to install it. It runs only when you press OK; nothing checks in the background.
strings.help.pref.language: The language of Hearth's menus. Left and right switch between the bundled languages; the texts in them are mostly machine translated. On a rooted TV, OK loads your own language file (a .json file from a USB drive or the folder /media/developer/languages); a wrong file changes nothing and the pop-up says why. The format is described in the language pack guide.
strings.help.pref.languageRemove: Deletes the language file you loaded and takes it out of Hearth. The menus go back to English. Bundled languages are not touched, and you can load a file again at any time.
strings.help.pref.tvApps: For TVs without root. Reads the list of apps from the TV through LG's own connection, so the home row can show your apps. It needs LG Connect Apps switched on in the TV's network settings (Mobile Connection Management). It is experimental and does not work on every webOS version. Rooted TVs do not need it.
strings.help.pref.noRootGuide: Without root, LG Home cannot be replaced, so Hearth cannot open by the Home button alone. OK shows two ways to reach Hearth quickly anyway: put it on one of LG's Quick Access buttons (1 to 9), or run a small watcher on a second device that opens Hearth when LG Home appears. Read-only; nothing is changed on the TV.
strings.help.pref.tvInput: Lists Hearth next to HDMI 1 in the TV's input list, so you can switch to it like an input. If you set the TV to start on its last input, the TV boots straight into Hearth. Rooted TVs only.
strings.help.pref.samHome: A second way to replace LG Home: Hearth mounts a stand-in over LG Home, so pressing Home opens Hearth instead. It may restart the TV's app manager, which closes running apps for a moment. Use it only if the other ways do not work for you. Experimental.
strings.help.pref.powerOnApp: The app the TV opens when it is switched on, instead of Live TV or the last input. Pick Hearth or any other app. It takes effect after one TV restart, because the TV reads the setting at boot. Rooted TVs only.
strings.help.pref.lgLogo: LG's own switch for the logo shown while the TV starts. Hearth only flips LG's own setting; it does not change how long the TV needs to boot. Not available on every TV.
strings.help.pref.homeApp: Registers Hearth as the TV's Home app, so the TV's own Home setting points to Hearth. It worked on webOS 4.x and did not work on webOS 7.x, so try it only on an older TV and keep it off otherwise. Experimental. Undo all system changes puts the old value back.
strings.help.pref.preload: Choose which LG apps the TV keeps loaded in the background, so they open faster when you start them. Every app you tick uses TV memory, so tick only the ones you really use. Experimental; if the TV becomes slow, untick them again.
strings.help.pref.keepReady: Keeps Hearth in the TV's memory so pressing Home brings it back at once instead of starting it again. The more you keep ready, the more TV memory Hearth uses, which can slow other apps on a TV with little memory. Experimental. Switch it off if the TV feels slower.
strings.help.pref.keepRelaunch: Loads Hearth again at start-up if the TV closed it while it was kept ready. It needs Keep Hearth ready to be on; on its own it does nothing. Experimental.
strings.help.pref.showDebug: Adds the Debug and Tests tabs to Settings. Debug shows technical facts about your TV and Hearth, and writes a report to /tmp/hearth-debug.txt; the Tests tab holds checks you run by hand. Turn it on only when you are reporting a problem or were asked to; the tabs do nothing on their own.
strings.help.group.Time and date: What the widget shows: the time format, AM or PM, and the date.
strings.help.group.Widget look: Size, font, colour, position and backdrop of the clock, date and weather.
strings.help.group.Weather: The temperature and conditions under the date. Needs internet.
strings.help.pref.wallpaper: A built-in background, your own picture or a slideshow. The preview shows it behind your home screen.
strings.help.pref.wallpaperFit: Fill crops the picture to the screen; Fit shows all of it.
strings.help.pref.interval: How long each slideshow picture stays up. Each visit: a new one after a restart or a minute away.
strings.help.pref.shuffle: Plays the slideshow in random order. Off plays A to Z.
strings.help.pref.wallpaperOpacity: How solid the picture is. Lower values soften it.
strings.help.pref.fadeStrength: Darkens the bottom of the picture so the icons stay easy to read.
strings.help.pref.homeFocus: Where the highlight starts when you come back to the home screen from another app. While you browse the row it stays where you put it.
strings.help.pref.widgetOn: Turns the clock, date and weather on or off. With it on, the Widget tab shows more rows and a live preview.
strings.help.pref.resetLook: Puts theme, wallpaper, look, quiet mode, clock and weather back to their defaults. Favourites, their order, the apps on the home row and the screen saver are not touched.
strings.help.pref.essentialsEdit: Choose which rows appear in Essentials.
strings.help.pref.homeKey: Makes the Home button open Hearth directly, so LG Home does not flash. Hearth uses its bundled key hook for this and finds the button code itself; if another tool already uses the Input Hook, these rows grey out. Needs root. This is the cleanest way to replace LG Home.
strings.help.pref.remap: Give another remote button a job: open an app, switch to an input, act as another button or run a TV action. Home, arrows, OK, Back, power, volume, channels and numbers cannot be mapped. Mapped buttons work through Hearth's bundled key hook, so they need root. Actions marked experimental may not work on every TV; tell us which ones do.
strings.help.pref.replaceHome: A small helper runs on the TV and opens Hearth whenever LG Home comes to the front. LG Home can flash briefly first, except when the Home button is mapped (Map home button). Rooted TVs only.
strings.help.pref.screensaver: Replaces the TV screen saver with your own pictures, GIFs, videos or a slideshow. Rooted TVs only and experimental; if the set-up fails, it switches itself off and says why.
strings.help.pref.screensaverPictures: Chooses what the saver plays: the built-in photos or video, one of your own pictures, GIFs or videos, or a whole folder as a slideshow. Rooted TVs only.
strings.help.pref.screensaverInterval: How long each picture stays on screen in a slideshow before the next one comes. Shown only for a slideshow.
strings.help.pref.screensaverShuffle: Plays the slideshow in random order. Off plays the pictures in name order, A to Z. Shown only for a slideshow.
strings.help.pref.screensaverCare: Moves a thin frame slowly around the picture so a still image does not burn into an OLED screen. Best left on for a single picture.
strings.help.pref.screensaverFit: Fit shows the whole picture, with black bars where it does not match the screen. Fill covers the whole screen and crops what does not fit.
strings.help.pref.screensaverDim: Darkens the saver pictures by the chosen amount, which is gentler on an OLED screen and in a dark room. Bright shows them unchanged.
strings.help.pref.screensaverPowerOff: Switches the TV off after the saver has run for this long. Off lets the saver run until you press a key.
strings.help.pref.screensaverShow: Starts the saver right now so you can try your settings.
strings.help.pref.quietSec: Hides the apps after the chosen time without a key press, and any key brings them back. Dimming and switching the TV off after a while can be added below. Off turns it off.
strings.help.pref.scrollSpeed: How fast the home row moves while Left or Right is held down, and while the Magic Remote pointer rests at the edge of the row.
strings.help.pref.undoAll: Takes back every change Hearth made on the TV: start-up links, folders, screen saver, button settings, the Home app. It writes one log file, then uninstalls Hearth. Your own wallpaper, theme and language folders stay. The TV may restart at the end. Use it before removing Hearth for good.
